text:
sam: FYI ACME reported a sudden p95->p99 regression ~02:10 UTC. They see requests stuck in waitlist for 10-30s and then 504s. Ticket #12345. Repro: 1) curl POST /v1/generate with tenant API key 2) repeated bursts ~200rps for 30s 3) observe long queueing + occasional 401s. Can we triage?

jules: Thanks Sam — customer is getting anxious. Do we have an ETA? I relayed were investigating and asked them for logs.

priya: Looking at ingress metrics now. prod-gpu-pool-3 request_queue_length spiked from ~50 to 120 around 02:08 UTC, concurrency saturation on pool-3 workers. Also saw backlog in admission-controller.

marco: Admission-controller logs show worker eviction events and pod restarts between 02:05-02:20. A subset of nodes hit OOMKilled, then kubelet restarted pods -> temporary capacity loss.

priya: Sample from ingress logs:```
[02:09:12] tenant=acme req_id=abc123 queue_pos=87 admit=false reason=pool-saturated
[02:09:14] tenant=acme req_id=abc124 admit=true latency_ms=3120
[02:09:20] tenant=acme req_id=abc125 error=504 downstream_timeout
```

nadia: We rolled a small model canary (model v2.1) to ~10% of GPU fleet at 02:15 UTC for perf testing. I see pods for v2.1 with higher memory usage on nodes n-07..n-11. A few went CrashLoopBackOff.

priya: That matches — increased memory footprint from v2.1 caused OOMs and reduced available worker slots, which made admission controller pile up requests. Root cause seems memory regression in v2.1.

sam: Customer asked for mitigation ASAP. Can we rollback and/or route ACME to a different pool/dedicated capacity?

priya: Immediate plan: 1) rollback canary -> revert v2.1 2) temporarily pin ACME to higher priority queue + increase their per-tenant concurrency cap 3) enable burst routing to dedicated if capacity remains constrained. I'm initiating the rollback now.

svc-deploy-bot: Rollback started by priya at 02:40 UTC — reverting model rollout to v2.0 across canary nodes.

marco: After rollback we see reduced OOM events. Queue length down from 120 -> 22 within ~6 minutes. p95 improved but p99 still slightly elevated due to queued backlog and retry storms. Recommend temporary bump of worker concurrency (per-process) and enabling priority admissions for enterprise tenants while backlog drains.

priya: Applied transient policy: pinned tenant=acme to priority_queue and increased tenant_concurrency=32 for 15m. Also increased admission-queue depth for pool-3 by 50%.

jules: I messaged the customer: "We reverted a canary causing memory regressions and pinned your traffic to a higher-priority path. Expect improvements in ~10-15m. Will update once stable."

sam: Customer reports latency much better now, but seeing a handful of 401 auth errors during their retry window. Any idea?

priya: Auth service had a short rate-limit spike around the same time (too many retries for failed calls). I increased token cache TTL and added jitter to retry logic for the client-facing SDK to avoid thundering-herd token refreshes. Also adjusted auth rate-limit thresholds temporarily.

marco: Post-mitigation metrics: p95 back to baseline, p99 within 10% of baseline. No new OOMs. Action items: 1) full postmortem (assign later) 2) add rollout circuit-breaker to prevent canary with memory regression from hitting admission controller 3) better per-tenant admission telemetry and SLA alerts.

jules: I'll follow up with customer and offer interim credits if they request. Also capturing their repro to include in postmortem.

sam: Great work team. Closing loop when p99 is stable for 1h. :thumbsup:
